'''Dr. Joseph B. Schlenoff''' is a distinguished research professor and [[Leo Mandelkern]] Professor of Polymer Science of the department of chemistry and biochemistry at [[Florida State University]]. He graduated with his doctorate in chemistry from [[UMass-Amherst]] in 1987 and became a professor at Florida State University in 1988.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dgr.rints.com/faculty.cfm?id=S0009497 |title=American Chemical Society |website=dgr.rints.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921055704/http://dgr.rints.com/faculty.cfm?id=S0009497 |archive-date=2013-09-21}} </ref> A leading scientist in the field of water-soluble polymers and biocompatible polymer composites and blends, Dr. Schlenoff has discovered a process for creating biomaterials that can be used in surgical implants designed for the extended release of certain medications and holds 30 issued and many pending patents.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://fsucom.thinkcreative.com/More-FSU-News/Chemist-earns-prestigious-Florida-Award-from-American-Chemical-Society |title=Chemist earns prestigious Florida Award from American Chemical Society / More FSU News - FSU.com |accessdate=2014-10-08 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104044732/http://fsucom.thinkcreative.com/More-FSU-News/Chemist-earns-prestigious-Florida-Award-from-American-Chemical-Society |archivedate=2013-11-04 }}</ref> This number of issued patents places him second among faculty at Florida State University behind only [[Robert A. Holton]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fsu.edu/profiles/schlenoff/ |title=Joseph B. Schlenoff |website=www.fsu.edu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060830211601/http://www.fsu.edu/profiles/schlenoff/ |archive-date=2006-08-30}} </ref> He is the founder of the start-up, nanoStrata, a company that manufactures novel robots to create biofilms.<ref>[http://floridatrend.com/extra_article.asp?page=7&extraID=17&aID=48509 University Spin Game – University of Florida]</ref> Dr. Schlenoff was one of three researchers from around the world awarded a Gutenberg Chair for 2011 at the [[Université de Strasbourg]] in France.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://news.fsu.edu/More-FSU-News/News-Archive/2011/April/Chemistry-professor-Joseph-Schlenoff-awarded-prestigious-Gutenberg-Chair-at-Universite-de-Strasbourg |title=Gutenberg Chair at the Universite de Strasbourg |access-date=2013-09-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921061930/http://news.fsu.edu/More-FSU-News/News-Archive/2011/April/Chemistry-professor-Joseph-Schlenoff-awarded-prestigious-Gutenberg-Chair-at-Universite-de-Strasbourg |archive-date=2013-09-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2013, Dr. Schlenoff was awarded the Florida Award from the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://fsucom.thinkcreative.com/Watch-and-Listen/Radio-Stories/Chemist-earns-prestigious-Florida-Award-from-American-Chemical-Society |title=2013 Florida Award |access-date=2013-09-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921061933/http://fsucom.thinkcreative.com/Watch-and-Listen/Radio-Stories/Chemist-earns-prestigious-Florida-Award-from-American-Chemical-Society |archive-date=2013-09-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
